verses.1: After that, the Lord showed them seventeen others. He sent them out in pairs, before his own face, to go to every city and place where he intended to go.
verses.2: He said to them, “The work is very difficult, and there are few workers available. Therefore, you need to ask the master of the work to assign some workers to carry out his work.”
verses.3: Go ahead; I’ll send you out as messengers in the midst of wolves.
verses.4: Do not wear bavarian clothes, do not carry anything, and do not defend anything along the way.
verses.5: You say that you first entered the house into which they went. Peace to this house.
verses.6: And if there is a son of peace there, then the peace between you will be restored to him. But if not, then it will be restored to you.
verses.7: Stay in this house, eating and drinking what is provided for you there. After all, the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from one house to another.
verses.8: And in the city where you enter, they will welcome you. Then, you may eat whatever is offered to you.
verses.9: And you also heal those who are sick among them. You say to them, “The kingdom of God is coming over you.”
verses.10: If they refuse to welcome you when you enter their city, then go into the streets of that city and say:
verses.11: And we will throw the scroll that has been attached to us from your city onto your feet. But besides this, remember that it is the kingdom of God that will be established.
verses.12: I tell you that Sodom will be more affected by this day than the city itself.
verses.13: Do not be afraid, Chorazin; do not be afraid, Bithsaida. For even if such forces occurred in Tyre and Sidon, they would have been forgotten long ago, just like those who sat in ashes and dust.
verses.14: In addition, Tyrus and Sidon will be given a longer time to make their case before you judge them.
verses.15: And you too, Kafarnauum, will not be raised up until you reach the heavens. You will be brought down to the depths of darkness.
verses.16: He who hears you hears me too; and he who dislikes you dislikes me as well. But he who dislikes me dislikes the person who sent me there.
verses.17: They returned after seventy-two days, happy and saying, “Lord, even the demons are under your control in your name.”
verses.18: He said to them, “Look at Satan as a drop that fell from heaven.”
verses.19: I have given you the authority to rule over all infants and lambs, as well as over all those who are under the power of the enemy. I will not harm any of you in any way.
verses.20: But besides this, you shouldn’t be happy that your spirits are subdued by them. Instead, you should be happy that your names are recorded in the heavens.
verses.21: In that time, he became united with the holy spirit. He said, “I confess to you, Father of heaven and earth, that I have hidden these things from the wise and good, and revealed them to the foolish. But, Father, it was good for me to do so.”
verses.22: It has always been revealed to me by my father. No one knows who the son is, unless he himself reveals it. And no one knows who the father is, unless the son reveals it as well.
verses.23: And he also spoke privately to his students, saying, “Blessed are those who see what you see.”
verses.24: I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but they did not see it; and they wanted to hear what you hear, but they did not hear it.
verses.25: And someone from the legal community stood up and asked him, “Teacher, what should I do in order to inherit eternal life?”
verses.26: And he said to him, “What is written in the law? How can you know?”
verses.27: And the one who replied said, “You must love your Lord God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind. And you must treat those who are near to you as yourself.”
verses.28: He said to him, “You have spoken truthfully. Thus, he will live and act accordingly.”
verses.29: And he who wanted to gain his own rights said to Jesus, “Who are those who are near me?”
verses.30: When Jesus heard this, he said, “If anyone were to go from Jerusalem to Jericho and get into the hands of robbers, they would surely leave him there, wounded, and unable to get away.”
verses.31: But along the way, a priest went down the road with him. When he saw him, he turned around and faced him.
verses.32: Similarly, Leuites also came to that place, and when he saw his opponent, he turned around and fought against him.
verses.33: And a Samaritan, while walking along that road, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
verses.34: And when he arrived, he treated his wounds by applying oil and wine. After that, he took him to a comfortable place where he was cared for properly.
verses.35: And on the fourth day, he gave two denarii to the host, and said, “Be careful with this. If you do anything wrong, I will return those denarii to you when I leave.”
verses.36: Do you think that among these three, one of them has become like those who were trapped in the hands of the thieves?
verses.37: And he said, “You too, do the same kind deeds with him.” Jesus replied to him, “You also, go and do the same.”
verses.38: While they were traveling, he himself entered a certain city. There, a woman named Martha took care of him.
verses.39: And there was also a sister named Maria, who sat beside Jesus’ feet. She heard His words.
verses.40: And Martha devoted herself to many duties. When she returned, she said, “Lord, don’t you know that it’s only my sister who is left to take care of me?” So he told her to arrange for someone else to take care of me.
verses.41: Then the Lord replied to her, “Mary, Mary! You are full of worries and noise about many things.”
verses.42: It’s not much of a problem for just one person. For Maryam, she was chosen to receive the good portion, and that portion will not be taken away from her.
